en: The Ritual for the Practice and Accomplishment of Mahāsukha-Vajrasattva, in one fascicle.
Extracted from the *Śrīparamādya-tantra-rāja-yoga-sūtra*.
By the Grand Master of the Court, Peer of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra, Śramaṇa of Daixingshan Monastery, who held the title of Grand Preceptor, was granted the purple robe and the posthumous rank of Minister of Works, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Sugu with a fief of three thousand households; he received imperial edict to translate this work. I take refuge in Vajrasattva, who can expound the gateway of the three vajra secrets.
For the sake of those who practice the conduct and words of the Bodhisattva path,
they shall not undergo toil and suffering, but shall instead correspond with peace and bliss;
for by means of sublime skillful means, they will swiftly achieve accomplishment.
I shall now explain it.
A practitioner should first give rise to this thought:
"I shall bring peace, happiness, and benefit to the entire realm of sentient beings without exception."
In order to accomplish this mind,
one should recite the mantra of the naturally accomplished nature as desired. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvayogacittam utpādayāmi. By merely giving rise to this thought and reciting the mantra, all obstacles are severed.
One shall obtain all peace, happiness,
and joy; neither the hosts of māras nor sentient beings who are difficult to subdue will be able to create obstacles.
He is equal to Perfect Enlightenment and should receive the vast offerings of all the world’s humans and devas.
Next, one contemplates that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature.
This is called having already cultivated the bodhicitta;
one then dwells in the contemplation of the Great Bodhicitta of Samantabhadra.
Just as the full moon is pure white and distinct, one further visualizes the lunar disc above it.
It surged upward to form a five-pronged vajra,
its radiance brilliant and translucent;
this vajra then transformed into Vajrasattva himself.
Her form is like the full moon, adorned with all manner of ornaments;
she wears a precious crown of the five Buddhas upon her head,
and her body, draped in crimson flames, rests upon a white lotus.
Next, perform the consecration with the Great Seal and the Heart Mantra.
As for the seal-form:
sit in the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka) with the right foot pressing upon the left.
Form the vajra-fist with both hands;
place the left at the hip and make a gesture of hurling with the right, pressing it against the heart.
With the vajras of body, speech, and mind, sit upright with the body straightened and recite the heart mantra:
HŪṂ. Next, form the mudrā of the vajra-palms joined.
For the mudrā of the firm palms, the mantra for the initial joining of the fingers is:
*Vajrañjali*. Next, bind the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*) mudrā.
Form the mudrā with the vajra-palms, then deeply interlace them into a fist. The mantra is:
VAJRA-BANDHA. This is the mudrā for all samayas.
All arise from this bondage.
Next, perform the heart-seal (*hṛdaya-mudrā*).
To open the seal and release the preceding bondage, recite the mantra for striking one's own heart:
By reciting *vajra-bandha-traṭ* and striking one's own heart,
all mudrās are bound;
one thereby attains mastery over the vajras of one’s own body, speech, and mind.
Next, bind the Vajra-Praveśa-Samaya-mudrā.
The form of the mudrā is the vajra-bind:
bend the two thumbs and insert them into the palms.
Placing [the thumb] between the ring finger and the little finger, the mantra is:
*Vajrāveśa* (1) *Aḥ* (2). By the empowerment of this mudrā, all the holy ones enter pervasively into the body and mind.
The empowerment and protective mindfulness are equal to those of a close friend.
Next, bind the Samaya-Vajra-Fist Mudrā;
its form is as the previous mudrā.
Bend the two index fingers and press them against the backs of the thumbs;
the mantra is: *vajramuṣṭiṃ hūṃ*. Next, form the *vajranetra-mudrā*.
For the mudrā, divide the previous mudrā into two fists.
Holding the left [fist] at the navel and placing the right against the heart, recite the Heart Mantra:
HŪṂ. Next, bind the Vajra-Guhyasamaya Mudrā.
Form the Vajrabandha mudrā;
with the thumbs and index fingers forming a hollow,
press the tip of the right thumb against it.
The mantra for the empowerment of the heart, forehead, throat, and crown is:
*sūtradhāraṇa*. Next, form the seal of the five Buddha consecrations (*pañcabuddhābhiṣeka-mudrā*).
The form of the seal is the vajra-palms-joined gesture (*vajra-añjali*).
Join the middle fingers and bend their third joints like swords.
Place each of the two index fingers alongside the third joint of a middle finger.
Cross the two thumbs in the form of a full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Place them on the crown of the head, followed by the forehead, the right side of the head, the back of the head, and the left side.
Recite the mantras of the five Buddhas to empower them; the mantra of Vairocana Tathāgata is as follows:
Oṃ bhu khaṃ. This is the mantra of Akṣobhya Tathāgata.
Vajrasattva. This is the mantra of Ratnasambhava Tathāgata. Vajraratna. This is the mantra of Amitābha Tathāgata.
The mantra of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, Vajradharma, is:
VAJRA KARMĀ. Next, form the Vajramālā mudrā.
Form two vajra-fists with the mudrā;
at the forehead and behind the crown of the head,
make the gesture of binding a garland.
Gradually let it flow down from the little finger, like a hanging silk ribbon. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajramālāviśuddhe maṃ. Having performed the consecration as before, [proceed].
Thereupon, one performs the consecration by sprinkling [the water] with the Vajrasattva empowerment.
Next, one binds the Mudrā of Joy.
As for the form of the mudrā, one extends both hands and claps them together; the mantra is as follows:
Vajra-tuṣya hūṃ. By means of this mudrā and the empowerment of this mantra,
they are released from their bonds and filled with joy,
attaining the essence of Vajrasattva.
Next, bind the vajreśvara mudrā and silently recite the following mantra once:
*savaṃ kuru* (1) *yathā suḥ khaṃ* (2). Then, visualize [the syllable] within the crown upon your head.
Each of the five Buddhas abides according to their respective original colors and forms,
maintaining their original mudras and postures,
and sits with full vajra-paryaṅka.
The Tathāgata Vairocana at the crown of the head is white in color.
With both fists, he extends the left thumb;
with the right fist, he grasps the first phalanx of the thumb against his heart.
In front is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, blue in color.
His left fist holds the corner of his robe against his heart;
his right hand extends its fingers with the palm facing downward.
With the fingertips of his right hand touching the ground upon his right knee,
he is yellow in color like the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava;
his left fist is as before, while his right palm is turned upward in the gesture of granting boons (*varada-mudrā*).
Behind him is Amitābha Tathāgata, red in color;
his left fist holds the stem of a lotus with pride, and his right fist opens it. To the left is Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata, green in color.
The left fist is as before, held at the heart;
the right thumb and index finger are joined together;
in the gesture of rescuing, the palm is raised near the breast.
Having performed the empowerment in this manner,
one’s own body shall become the essence of Vajrasattva.
Next, bind the随心印 (Sui-xin-yin) of the Great Bliss Vajra Amoghasamaya.
For the mudrā, perform the vajra-bind:
bend the middle fingers and insert them into the palms;
extend the thumbs and little fingers so that they touch one another.
Like a single-pronged vajra,
bend the two middle fingers into the shape of a hook and hook the heart.
Then, interlace the tips of the middle fingers like a cord and hook them deeply together like a chain;
shaking this chain against the chest constitutes the *ghaṇṭā* (bell) mudrā.
The mantra for the invocation is as follows:
*Oṃ mahā-sūkṣma-vajra-sattva-mahī-ṣṭi samaya mahā-sūkṣma-vajra-mukha*.
1. Samaya, 2. amanojñāya, 3. pramodāya pramodāya, 4.
suratāt sattva, 5. manorathaprabhava, 6. sustuṣṭiprabhava.
9. *su-dhṛti-vāba* 10. *su-pratiṣṭhita-vāba* 11.
*bhagavan* 12. *nānā-jñāna-sattva* 13. *sarva-siddhi-vā* 14. *prāyaccha īśatva*
dvau ṇakṛṣya praveśaya samayārādhana vaśīkaromi maitrā-mudrā-pūrṇa-dānaḥ.
Twenty: *ra*. Twenty-one: *hūṃ*. Twenty-two: *haiṃ*. Twenty-three: *hoḥ*. Twenty-four:
Visualize that all the honored ones assemble within the maṇḍala;
with the hook, one should contemplate their descent and arrival.
When one reaches the *suo* (lasso), one enters;
when one reaches the *suo* (chain), one can stop;
when one reaches the *qing* (gong), one is made joyful.
Contemplate clearly that Vajrasattva resides within the central mandala,
surrounded and honored by all the deities.
Next, fill a new and clean vessel with scented water.
Place flowers floating on water within the mandala,
near the left and right knees,
and empower them with the *argha* mudrā.
For the mudrā, join the palms in the vajra-joined-palms gesture (*vajrasaṃpuṭa*).
Extend the two middle fingers so they touch each other,
and bend the two index fingers into the shape of a hook.
With the two thumbs pressing against the bases of the two index fingers,
perform the empowerment by twisting the seal sideways while reciting the mantra of the syllable *Oṃ*.
Then, holding the *argha* vessel near the forehead, the mantra for the offering is as follows:
*paramasukhaśāye sārīta vilāsana-maitrāṇa maṃ bhagavan dhan hūṃ haḥ hi hi hi hi pratyakṣa kusumāñjali-ratata*. Having thus made the offering:
Next, one visualizes the deities.
Using their respective *karma-mudrās* and root mantras,
each is established in their assigned seat within the maṇḍala.
First, one should visualize a moon disc and then contemplate its form and color.
Next, the five secrets are taught: Vajrasattva.
Seated upon a white lotus pedestal,
he dwells with dignified majesty;
his form and appearance are as previously described, and he abides in the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) of the Vajra-Arrow.
The red-colored one resides in front, holding a bow and arrows;
Vajrarati is white and is situated on the right.
The essence of the robe-samaya is Vajrarāga;
all its attributes are blue.
In the rear position, he holds the Makara banner;
Vajrakāmeśvara is yellow in color and resides on the left.
The two fists are placed against the temples,
with their heads slightly tilted toward the left.
Now, the mudrās and mantras shall be explained.
Vajrasattva establishes [the practitioner] by means of the Vajrāñjali mudrā and the heart mantra,
employing two vajra-fists.
The mantra for the posture of drawing the bow and releasing the arrow is:
*Vajra-tiṣṭha sañjaya kīlaya svāhā*. Furthermore, the mantra for crossing the two fists at the chest and embracing them is: [as above].
HŪṂ VAJRA HAKĀRI KĪLI HŪṂ. Again, with both fists, place the left near the right breast,
then bend the right elbow and rest it upon the left fist.
The mantra for raising the arms like a banner is:
*HŪṂ Vajri samara raṭa ṭa*. Furthermore, place both fists at the hips.
Bowing with the head turned to the left and slightly lowered, the mantra is:
*Hūṃ vajrakāminī svāhā*. Next, the inner offerings for the four corners are explained.
The Vajra of Wondrous Delight;
pure white offerings of flowers;
the nature of Vajra Delight.
The Black-colored [deity] burns various incenses in a furnace;
Vajranetra wears red garments and is worshipped with lamps.
Vajra-Mahāśrī is yellow in color and holds fragrant ointment;
now the mudrās and mantras for these four inner offerings shall be explained.
First, perform the dance with two vajra-fists,
and thereafter form the mudrā;
first, place both fists together with palms facing downward.
Then, turning the palms upward in the gesture of scattering flowers, the mantra is:
*HĪ VAJRA RATI*. Next, joining both fists together and opening them downward in the gesture of burning incense, the mantra is: [Mantra for burning incense].
*Mahāratnavajrī*. [Gestures: Both hands joined in fists;
extend the tips of the thumbs and join them together. The mantra for the lamp is:
*Oṃ vajra-dīpa-jaḥ*. [Gestures: Both hands joined in fists.
Spreading [the offerings] from the chest outward in both directions as if applying fragrant unguents, the mantra is:
*Mahāśrī-vajri hīḥ*. Then, perform the outer offerings to the four corners.
Vajralāsyā, Vajrahāsā, Vajragītā, and Vajranṛtyā—
these four outer offerings are all made of pure gold.
Now, the mudrās and mantras shall be explained.
Form two fists with the backs joined and placed against the heart, turning to the right.
The mantra for the Playful Sport (*līlā*) is:
*kṣitidhara vajra vilāsini tandraṭaṭa*. Again, form two fists with the backs joined and placed [at the heart].
Lift the thumb to the mouth.
Slowly release from the little finger.
With a slight smile, recite the mantra as follows:
Recite *kīlita-vajra hāse ha ha*. Then, with both fists, extend the index fingers slightly bent;
raise the left arm so that it forms the shape of a lute (*vīṇā*).
The mudrā for snapping the string with the right index finger has the mantra:
*kīlaya vajra hūṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭha*. Furthermore, one should place both fists at the heart and perform a whirling dance.
Then, with an empty mind, join the palms together and scatter them above the crown of the head while reciting this mantra:
*kīra ti vajra nṛtye ve pa ve pa*. Next, explain the four gates for receiving instructions.
The vajra hook is in front and is blue in color;
the vajra noose is on the right and is yellow in color;
the vajra chain is at the back and is red in color.
The vajra-bell is on the left and is green in color.
Now, the mudrās and mantras will be explained.
Hook the little fingers of both fists together.
Interlace the wrists and extend both index fingers straight upward;
then, slightly bending the right index finger, use it to beckon as a hook. The mantra is as follows:
Vajra-kuśa (1) [the gesture of the hook]. Again, according to this, for the hook-seal (ākarṣaṇa-mudrā), the two index fingers are joined like a cord. The mantra is:
Vajrapāśa hūṃ (1). Furthermore, this is the same as the cord-seal (pāśa-mudrā).
Change it by interlocking the two index fingers.
Opening the backs of the hands to form a lock, the mantra is:
*vajraśṛṅkhalī hūṃ*. Furthermore, this is the aforementioned lock-seal (*śṛṅkhalā-mudrā*).
Place the backs of the two hands together and shake them up and down; this is the *kṣepaṇa* mantra:
*vajra-yantra-hūṃ*. From the second line onwards, all sixteen deities are to be visualized with eyes full of joy.
Behold Vajrasattva,
who bears the five buddhas upon his crown;
each sits in the sattvaparyaṅka posture upon a moon disc.
Their crowns, garlands, and garments follow the colors of their respective bodies.
Next, the samaya-mudrās of the various sages are displayed,
beginning with Vajrasattva.
Next, bind the previously mentioned Vajra-Guhyasamaya-mudrā and recite the mantra:
*sūtradastvaṃ*. Then, bind the previously mentioned Mahāsukha-vajra-amoghasamaya-cittānugata-mudrā.
Bend the backs of the two index fingers so they touch like arrow feathers,
and press down with both thumbs;
clench the fist to form the Vajra-Arrow Mudrā.
Furthermore, for the arrow mudrā:
interlace the two thumbs deeply, with the right pressing over the left; this is the Vajra-joy mudrā.
Furthermore, for the preceding mudrā,
interlace the two index fingers with the middle fingers and place the thumbs side by side on the sides of the index fingers like ears.
Extend the two ring fingers and join them together to form the Vajraprema-mudrā (Vajra-Love Seal).
Next, twist the previous seal sideways and place it upon the two thighs—
first the right, then the left— to form the Vajrakāmeśvara-mudrā (Vajra-Lust Sovereign Seal).
Next, twist the fingers of the vajra palms together at the heart;
cast them as flowers to scatter downward while offering incense;
then change the position so that the two thumbs are joined together.
The "Small Opened Palm" is called the Lamp;
it is held against the chest with both hands spread outward.
The "Ointment Incense" is performed in the manner of applying ointment incense.
Next, perform the side-twisted vajra-joined palms;
as before, rotate them to the right at the heart for "playful sport.
Bringing them near the mouth and spreading them from the little fingers is called "laughter."
Slightly bend both index fingers.
The left index finger is shaped like a *vīṇā* lute, while the right index finger is held in the posture of plucking a string; this is called "Song."
As before, perform three turns to the right with the *khaṭakā* hand gesture,
dancing as previously described.
Next, form the *vajrabandha*, extend the right index finger, and slightly bend it.
Slowly beckon with it as a hook.

Using the tip of the left thumb to press against the left "tiger's mouth" (the base of the index finger) is called "binding the left. Then, pinch the tip of the index finger together with the tip of the thumb.
The right hand likewise forms the lock;
bend both thumbs and each grasp the space between the ring finger and the little finger.
Shake it, calling it the *qing* (stone chime).
With the *samaya-mudrā* of the sixteen honored ones mentioned previously,
recite the preceding *karma-mantra* for each.
Having established the deities as previously arranged,
one should visualize Vajrasattva with sixteen deities as his retinue;
the practitioner then abides in the yoga of his own chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā).
There are also sixteen deities surrounding him.

Next, recite the King of Praises (*stotra-rāja*), which consists of four lines: *Sarvanurāga-sukha-sattvānāṃ vajrasattva-pramokṣa-kara |* *Svāmin mahāsukha-dhṛk jaya pratisiddhāna-śiṣya-cara-gotrata ||* This praise has four verses.
Recite the first line while forming the arrow mudrā;
the second line with the joy mudrā;
and the third line with the love mudrā.
For the fourth line, one binds the Seal of Sovereignty over Desire and simultaneously binds the aforementioned Karma-mudrā;
this is because of chanting this King of Praises.
Great bliss, great compliance, love, delight,
and satisfaction are all attained as desired and become firm.
Furthermore, recite this most excellent praise of reality:
Mahā-sūkṣma (1) Mahā-rāga (2) Mahā-vajra (3) Mahā-dhana (4) Mahā-kīrtana (5) Mahā-karma (6) Vajrasattva jñānasiddhyai svāhā (7). By reciting this praise, [one attains accomplishment].
This will enable one to swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, the eye mudrā is explained;
one should perform it as the Mahāsukha-vajra.
The Seal of Amoghasukha-avabodhana:
Its form consists of a great expression of bliss, with eyes blinking and a smiling face looking about.
By means of this seal, one swiftly attains accomplishment.
Furthermore, perform the seal of the Great Delightful Vajra-Āmogha-Arrow.
As for the form of the seal: the eyes are like blossoming flowers, half-closed, and one gazes with a smile.
With the left hand holding a *khaṭvāṅga* and the right hand performing three turns,
one then performs the ritual dance as prescribed.
Then, one performs the gesture of tossing flowers.
By the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of this mudrā, one abides as before.
Furthermore, one performs the Great Gesture of Gazing with Delight.
The mudrā is exceedingly pleasing to behold;
because it is so greatly pleasing to gaze upon,
even those of meager merit can achieve accomplishment.
Furthermore, perform the seal of the Great Delight Vajra Banner.
The form of the seal is such that the eyes are moved to the utmost, as if the heart were deeply stirred.
By means of this seal, one quickly attains accomplishment.
One should realize through direct experience that this [mudrā] surpasses all those of the non-Buddhists.
Furthermore, perform the mudrā of salutation;
its form is as described previously.
With an expression of being moved, the eyes move slightly;
the left hand forms the *khaṭaka* mudrā and the right hand performs the triple-flip (*tri-parivarta*),
whirling and dancing as before at the heart.
Afterwards, one performs the gesture of scattering flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).

Because of paying homage with this mudrā, all the world pays homage to this person and makes offerings to them. Regarding the meaning of "gazing at the Principal Deity" as previously mentioned: it refers to the act of looking up and gazing intently upon the Principal Deity while holding the mudrā.
The Great Sage is precisely the wisdom of the essential nature of the Dharma-realm.
To observe him now with a mind of longing and admiration is itself to behold the nature of perfect quiescence.
In all cases, assist with the *karma-mudrā* while reciting the root mantra.
Next, gaze with the eyes and perform the mudrā for inviting the deity to enter one's body.
Form the mudrā with the eyes slightly open, blinking and looking around.
Visualize that the Honored One enters completely into one’s body.
Next, form the mudrā for exhausting all attachment to body and mind.
That is to say, one should form this intention:
"I now, with all the attachment of my body and mind,
serve the noble Vajrasattva."
Because this seal enables one to abide in all realities by means of penetrating the nature of wisdom,
Vajrasattva abides in the wisdom of the essential nature of the dharmadhātu.
I shall now also decisively attain realization by means of this seal-convenience (*mudrā-upāya*).
Next, bind the Vajra-Blazing-Sun Samaya Seal.
For the mudrā, deeply interlace the two hands with the palms facing each other and slightly clench them into fists;
extend the eight fingers like flames.
Extend the two thumbs and join them together like a vajra;
rotate counterclockwise against the direction of the sun,
visualizing that those who are difficult to subdue are expelled.
Supporting the ground below, one binds the boundary of the earth;
turning to the right in accordance with the sun’s course,
one establishes the boundary at whatever distance is desired.
Above, visualize the formation of the realm of empty space;
recite the mantra *HŪṂ*.
Next, with the intention of one's own superior resolve...
One contemplates unguents, flower garlands, incense, food and drink, clothing, precious canopies, banners, pennants, fans, fly-whisks, exquisite dances, and palaces,
for the sake of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
I shall now manifest through transformation the ritual procedures, songs, and hymns of praise,
pervading the entire realm of space as an offering.
The mantra for reciting the syllable *Oṃ* is as follows:
*Oṃ karu muṃ khaṃ sarvadharmānāmānya nuttaraṃ dharmatattva*. By reciting this mantra, [the following occurs].
Visualize as before:
the enjoyment of all the holy ones is entirely sufficient,
no different from the reality itself.
If there are objects for offering and so forth,
one should likewise empower them with the aforementioned mantra and then abide in the Great Seal (mahāmudrā).
Furthermore, with the vajra-eye,
one gazes for a long time at the Great Sage Vajrasattva,
without moving the tip of the tongue excessively.
The lips and teeth should be joined together;
thus one accomplishes all the teachings of the Dharma.
Vajra speech is free from sound.
Just as in the previous samādhi, with one-pointed concentration and certainty,
through recitation you shall cause Vajrasattva to appear before you and enter pervasively into your body.
One immediately becomes the very body of the Honored One.
Whenever one recites and becomes utterly exhausted and wishes to cease,
one should do so with a mind of personal resolve.
Contemplate the aforementioned offerings and so forth;
recite the mantra of the syllable Oṃ and thereby present them.
Afterwards, recite the hymn of one hundred and eight names as follows:
If one holds this King of Praises, the Vajra Dharma-speech, and recites it as desired, one shall achieve accomplishment swiftly and peerlessly.
One should recite it at the proper time every day; having done so, one is freed from all sins.
May all suffering be forever liberated, and the Pure Land shall manifest before you.
Merely by reciting this, all merits are perfected; may auspiciousness and brilliance increase.
Furthermore, perform the empowerment of the *argha* water as previously described.
Offer these according to the Dharma.
Then, form the *karmamudrā* and *samayamudrā* of the various deities;
having completed all of them as before by reciting their respective root mantras, proceed as follows.
Next, bind the Vajra-Blazing Sun Samaya-mudrā.
Rotate it to the left while visualizing the dissolution of the boundary and recite the mantra:
HŪṂ. Next, bind the mudrā for the dismissal.
Form the mudrā of Vajrabandha by extending the two middle fingers straight upward,
joining them like a needle at the heart;
then recite the mantra for the respectful dismissal.
To conclude, raise the mudrā near the crown of the head;
first, open and spread the middle fingers.
Visualize the assembly of holy beings returning to their original palaces. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kṛto vaḥ sarvasattvarātrayaḥ siddhivandanatā yathānugaccheda brahma buddhaviśaye punar āgamanaṃ tu | Oṃ vajrasattva muḥ. Whenever one wishes to exit the maṇḍala:
Having empowered one's own body with the previously mentioned protection seal,
one may proceed as appropriate to practice the preliminary rites.
According to the ritual procedures as previously described,
recite one hundred thousand times four times daily until the prescribed limit of days is fulfilled.
Recite the mantra continuously throughout the night until dawn without interruption;
once the preliminary practice is perfected,
one may then perform the cultivation at any time according to one's capacity.
In this very life, you shall before long attain the body of the Great Bliss Vajrasattva.
Furthermore, the essential points of the ritual procedure are set forth.
Next, recite the mantra for generating the bodhicitta:
Oṃ sarvayogacittam utpādayāmi. One should then contemplate: "I am Vajrasattva."
Then, one forms the Vajreśvara mudrā;
the form of the seal is to sit in half-lotus posture with the left fist placed upon the hip.
Recite the mantra at the heart as follows:
HŪṂ. Next, bind the Vajra-Guhyasamaya-mudrā.
The form of the mudrā is the vajra-bind.
The thumb and index finger form the aperture.
The right thumb is pressed subtly.
The mantra for empowering the heart, forehead, throat, and crown is as follows:
Next, recite *sūtradhāraṇa* and form the seal of the five Buddhas’ consecration (*pañcabuddhābhiṣeka-mudrā*). The form of the seal is as follows:
join the palms in the vajra-pañjali gesture;
interlock the middle fingers and bend their third joints together like a sword.
Place the tips of the two index fingers against the third joints of the middle fingers.
Interlace the two thumbs in the shape of a *paryaṅka* (crossed legs).
Place [the mudrā] on the crown of the head, followed by the forehead, the right side of the head, the back of the head, and the left side of the head.
The mantra for empowering with the mantras of the five Buddhas is:
Oṃ bhuḥ vajrasattva vajraratna vajradharma vajrakarma. Next, bind the Vajramālā mudrā.
Form two vajra-fists with the hand-seals;
make the gesture of binding a garland at the forehead and behind the head,
then slowly release them from the little fingers downward.
The mantra for hanging the silk streamers is:
Oṃ vajramālāviśva maṃ. Having thus completed the formation of the body as before.
Then, one binds the *karmamudrā* of the eight offerings.
The form of the seal consists of two vajra-fists,
placed face down and joined side by side.
Hurling [the flowers] upward, they become blossoms;
scattering [the incense] downward, it becomes burning incense;
joining the thumbs together, they form a lamp.
Relying on the chest, the two hands gradually open toward each other as they apply the fragrant ointment;
covering the marks, they meet at the heart and turn to the right in playful sport.
As in this play, they draw near the mouth and slowly disperse to form a smile.
With both fists extended, raise the index fingers;
with the left arm held like a *vīṇā* lute, assume the posture of plucking the strings with the right hand while singing.
Perform a whirling dance at the heart center.
Forming the "empty-palms" gesture above the crown of the head constitutes the dance.
The mantras for the eight offerings are as previously explained in the extensive ritual manual.
Having completed the formation of the body according to the rite and the eight offerings, [the procedure concludes].
Next, one contemplates that all forms are empty.
Having reflected in this way,
one then employs words that are exquisite, pleasant, and delightful.
Recite the initial sound according to one's capacity—
namely, the syllable *A*— and contemplate that all phenomena are fundamentally unborn from the very beginning.
Furthermore, one should manifest as the body of Vajrasattva.
Furthermore, with a mind of resolute conviction, one should mentally visualize the objects of offering and so forth,
while reciting the syllable *Oṃ*;
thereafter, one should constantly recite the heart-mantra.
In this manner, for one month, two months, or even six months,
the objective sphere appears clearly;
or one beholds various Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and all manner of sublime phenomena.
At all times, whenever one perceives pleasing things or objects of adornment and the like,
one should practice the contemplation of emptiness regarding them all and re-establish them [as such].
Once all have been rendered pure,
recite the mantra of the syllable Oṃ to make offerings to the Honored One.
Next, contemplate the body as empty in nature.
This is precisely the beholding of Vajrasattva.
Once such a supreme resolution has been firmly established,
whatever objects are perceived by the eyes naturally become empty.
Furthermore, one should establish a single deity as the principal deity (iṣṭadevatā).
One's own defilements and obscurations are purified,
and one should likewise visualize oneself as Vajrasattva.
By means of such yoga,
one should practice as desired while walking, standing, sitting, or remaining still;
furthermore, one should maintain the recitation of the mantra for one hundred thousand times.
On the final day, one should perform recitation throughout the night;
first accomplishing the preliminary practice,
one gradually increases one's diligent application of effort.
And in this very life, one will swiftly realize the wisdom of the Great Bliss Vajrasattva.
Regarding the rite of magnetizing (*vaśīkaraṇa*): first, visualize the gateway of the syllable *A* before oneself.
A pure lunar disc is formed.
Within that lunar disc, one visualizes the syllable *HŪṂ*,
which becomes the Bodhisattva Vajrarāga.
The body is the color of vermilion sand and emits red light;
with both hands, he holds arrows.
Having visualized this clearly, one recites the four-syllable mantra.
Form the mudrā and draw [the deity] into oneself.
The four-syllable mantra is:
*Jah Hūṃ Baṃ Hoḥ*. Then, empower the four places with the mudrā.
The mantras for the heart, forehead, throat, and crown are found in the *Vistara-sūtra*.
Oṃ vajrarāga ādhiṣṭhasva māṃ hūṃ. One should clearly visualize oneself as the Bodhisattva Vajrarāga.
Their deportment and physical appearance are indistinguishable;
one then visualizes that person standing one cubit in front of oneself,
with a syllable beneath their body.
It becomes a lotus flower.
He sees himself entering that person's body through the opening of the lotus.
It envelops his entire body and limbs as if he were wearing a robe;
observing his form from top to bottom, it is seen to be non-dual.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrarāgarāgaya [Name] hūṃ. While reciting this, one should contemplate its meaning with focused attention, maintaining an uninterrupted continuity for two full cycles of seven repetitions.
Thereafter, he beheld him;
whatever words were uttered were exactly those of that person, without any difference or distinction.
He sat cross-legged and upright, entering into meditative concentration.
Visualize before you the syllable A,
radiating brilliant light,
which then transforms into a lunar disc.
In the center of the wheel is the syllable HŪṂ.
Once it has been formed, he becomes the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa,
holding a hook in his two hands.
It then entered through the mouth and became a bodhisattva; immediately,
from within the heart, the syllable *ra* emerged.
Flowing like a garland, it enters directly into the heart of the beloved person,
becoming a hook,
just like a Vajra-woman.
Visualize the mind as a single pestle; the left hand is bent into a hook.
Contemplate the two bodies as non-dual.
